Here is my code review of the git diff:

===== HIGH SEVERITY ISSUES =====

1. Removal of v2store deprecation functionality without migration path
- Files: 
  - server/config/v2_deprecation.go (entire file deleted)
  - server/config/v2_deprecation_test.go (entire file deleted)
  - server/embed/config.go (lines 446-448 removed)
  - server/etcdmain/config.go (lines 55-58, 77, 97, 111, 164-182 removed)
  - server/etcdmain/help.go (lines 168-176 removed)
  - tests/e2e/v2store_deprecation_test.go (lines 26-34 removed)
- Evidence: Complete removal of v2store deprecation configuration and tests
- Risk: This removes functionality that was part of a planned deprecation path. Users may still have v2 data that needs to be migrated.

2. Removal of max-snapshots configuration without alternative
- Files:
  - etcd.conf.yml.sample (lines 28-30 removed)
  - server/config/config.go (lines 60-61 removed)
  - server/embed/config.go (lines 180-183 removed)
  - server/embed/etcd.go (line 191 removed)
  - server/etcdmain/config.go (lines 56, 97 removed)
  - server/etcdmain/config_test.go (lines 40, 61, 471-473 removed)
  - tests/e2e/etcd_config_test.go (lines 662-706 removed)
- Evidence: Complete removal of snapshot file limit configuration
- Risk: This could lead to unbounded disk usage for snapshots if not properly handled elsewhere

===== MEDIUM SEVERITY ISSUES =====

1. Hardcoded snapshot file limit
- File: server/etcdserver/server.go (lines 93-96, 598-602 added)
- Evidence: maxSnapDBFiles is now hardcoded to 5
- Risk: Loss of configurability for snapshot retention policy

===== LOW SEVERITY ISSUES =====

1. Documentation updates needed
- Files:
  - server/etcdmain/help.go (lines 73-74 removed)
  - etcd.conf.yml.sample (comment about snapshots removed)
- Evidence: Documentation not updated to reflect changes
- Risk: Users may be confused by missing configuration options

===== NON-CLAIM RISKS =====

1. Backward compatibility
- The removal of v2store deprecation configuration may break existing deployments that relied on this functionality

2. Testing coverage
- Several test files were removed without clear indication if equivalent tests were added elsewhere

3. Configuration flexibility
- Hardcoding the snapshot file limit reduces configuration flexibility that was previously available

The changes appear to be part of a planned deprecation path (references to v3.8 removal), but the complete removal of functionality without clear migration documentation or alternatives could cause issues for users. The snapshot configuration changes in particular seem risky as they could impact disk usage management.
